chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who has a servant who is the child of adultery; is there any blame upon him if he copulates with her? He said: No, and if he remains aloof from that, it is more beloved to me.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry or have relations with a female servant who is the child of adultery?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the lineage of illegitimacy (walad al-zina) does not constitute a barrier to marriage or sexual relations with a female servant, affirming the permissibility (jawaaz) without sin. However, he expresses a personal preference (hubb) for the man to remain aloof, highlighting the distinction between legal permissibility and spiritual or social virtue in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores that the 'bastard' retains full marital eligibility, distinguishing the child from those with specific impediments like mahram relationships.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who happened to have the maid for him born of adultery, would there be a blame upon him if he was to copulate with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, and if he was to remain aloof from that, so it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
was asked about the case of a man who has a servant born out of wedlock; if he can go to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, if he stays clean of that, it is more likeable to me.’”
